case: an epi state outside the model
why: The app colours the whole screen from this field; an unrecognised value has no colour and no safe default.
There is no defensible default. Assuming susceptible would tell an infected player they are healthy.
The score is the centre of the screen; absent is not the same as zero.
The game is scored in whole points; a fraction means a rule was applied that nobody designed.

case: protection expiry that is not UTC
why: The app counts down from this instant; an offset it misreads would expire protection at the wrong time.

case: a day before the game starts
why: Day counts forward from enrolment. A negative day would mean a tick ran for a period the study did not cover.
A zero-length game would divide by zero in every progress display and can only come from a misconfigured bundle.
Cumulative counts only rise. A negative one means the tick that produced it double-counted a recovery.

case: a field the app would silently ignore
why: Closed, so a server that starts sending something new fails loudly instead of being quietly dropped by every client.
The enumeration is what lets analysis separate a deliberate choice from a dead battery; a free-text source would make that distinction unusable.

case: a settlement line with no reason
why: An unexplained movement is exactly what the settlement exists to prevent.

case: a settlement reason the app cannot render
why: A player shown a movement they have no words for cannot check it.

case: a settlement with no opening balance
why: Without it the lines cannot be reconciled against anything.

case: a game said to last zero days
why: Null means open-ended; zero would mean a game that ended before it began, which nothing can render.
